changes.balance: Incident tempo and transit risk rose into the weekend without a measured flow change: the last volume gauge still puts strait crude at about half its pre-war rate, so the weekend reprices risk, not barrels, unless a gauge moves.
changes.body: An outbound tanker was struck on the stern about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab and a second was struck in the engine room about 17 nautical miles east of Khasab on Saturday morning (UKMTO, Nov 21). Specialist reporting identifies one casualty as the TORKEL, reported burning and anchored (NAVAREA IX 457/26, via DeepDraft, Nov 22). Iran's navy said a tanker hit a naval mine in a restricted area; Reuters could not verify that account and UKMTO's word in both warnings is projectile. The JMIC threat level remains SEVERE.
changes.conditional: A confirmed cargo loss, a terminal hit or a closure notice converts tempo into barrels and reprices the front on Monday; another quiet day on the gauges leaves the surplus framing and the positioning asymmetry in charge.
changes.delta: UKMTO Warnings 215-26 and 216-26 on Nov 21, at 0500 and 0550 UTC; no casualties, no closure, no confirmed cargo loss
changes.source: UKMTO Warnings 215-26 and 216-26, Nov 21, 2026; DeepDraft SITREP, Nov 22, 2026
changes.title: Two more tankers struck near Khasab on Saturday, three strikes in about fifteen hours

changes.balance: There is very little long length left to liquidate on a bearish headline, and a rebuilt short base in both contracts is squeeze fuel if a bullish headline lands, which makes Monday's reopen asymmetric against the weekend's incident tempo.
changes.body: Managed money WTI net length fell to +15,814 contracts, about 0.8 percent of open interest and the lowest net of 2026, with longs rising 5,519 while shorts were added to 137,797, the largest short book of the year (CFTC, released Nov 20). Brent managed money was essentially flat at +133,635 after two flush weeks from a September peak of +282,657.
changes.conditional: A Monday gap up on the weekend strikes forces short covering into a thin Thanksgiving week; a gap down has little length to feed on and fades unless a flow gauge confirms removed barrels.
changes.delta: WTI managed money net long +15,814 as of Nov 17, down 9,900 on the week, after 15,419 fresh shorts were added
changes.source: CFTC Commitments of Traders, released Nov 20, 2026
changes.title: Speculative length is at its lowest of 2026 and the short base is rebuilt

changes.balance: The bypass system that carried Gulf exports close to pre-war in October is now the system's centre of gravity, and its Red Sea outlet carries a named threat for the first time, which raises the value of the remaining routes without removing any barrels today.
changes.body: Arabian Gulf crude loadings in January to October 2026 were down 27.6 percent year on year and the Gulf share of global seaborne crude fell to 30.6 percent from 39.8 percent, with Fujairah and Yanbu, both reachable without transiting Hormuz, now the two largest loading terminals (Banchero Costa, reported Nov 21). The Houthi military spokesperson warned shipping companies to remove vessels from Saudi Red Sea ports, naming Jeddah, Yanbu, Jazan and King Fahd Industrial Port (DeepDraft, Nov 22); nothing has been hit and nothing has closed.
changes.conditional: Any strike on Yanbu or a Saudi port closure notice is a supply event against the bypass itself; threats without action stay a watch item and the re-based loading pattern stands.
changes.delta: Arabian Gulf loadings January to October down 27.6 percent year on year; Fujairah and Yanbu now ahead of Ras Tanura
changes.source: Banchero Costa weekly, reported Nov 21, 2026; DeepDraft SITREP, Nov 22, 2026
changes.title: Gulf loadings have re-based around the strait, and the bypass outlet is on a threat list
changes.vintage: Loadings January to October 2026; threat list Nov 22, 2026

flags.body: December Mainline apportionment (Light 24 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert) is announced for December. The Cromer and Superior points for December were not retrievable in any public source. The traded differential strip tightened for a fourth straight session into Friday, with January WCS paper settling -$21.65 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 20), and the balance residual is qualified against that pricing rather than carried as a storage forecast.
flags.title: December apportionment: Light 24 and Heavy 17 at Kerrobert
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment percentages as published in the notice itself

flags.body: Three Khasab-area tanker strikes landed in about fifteen hours across Friday and Saturday, with the JMIC threat level remaining SEVERE. The last measured strait clearance is 8.5 million barrels a day through Nov 16, about 50 percent of pre-war, while all-route Middle East oil ran at 15.0 million barrels a day, about 64 percent of pre-war and down from 97 percent in October. Wire lines that Hormuz shipments have returned to pre-war levels are not confirmed by these gauges for the strait itself, and Gulf loadings have re-based to terminals outside the strait.
flags.title: Hormuz gauges against the wire line
flags.trigger: A measured flow gauge (Kpler, Vortexa or UKMTO transit counts) confirming strait crude back at pre-war rates, or a confirmed cargo loss or closure

flags.body: The North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption has curtailed the system since Nov 14 with no restart timeline published. Producers were trucking Bakken crude to Dakota Access delivery points on Friday with tanks filling, and force majeure declarations stand at Flint Hills Pine Bend and at MPLX. The refinery receipt suspensions reported are of Bakken crude; no WCS buyer outage has been reported.
flags.title: North Dakota Pipeline disruption, day nine
flags.trigger: An Enbridge restart notice or a published restart timeline for the North Dakota Pipeline

flags.body: The Houthi military spokesperson warned shipping companies to remove vessels from Saudi Red Sea ports, naming Jeddah, Yanbu, Jazan and King Fahd Industrial Port as potential targets (DeepDraft, Nov 22). Yanbu is the Red Sea outlet of the East-West pipeline and the Gulf system's second-largest loading terminal. Nothing has been hit, nothing has closed and no evacuation order has been issued.
flags.title: Yanbu on a named threat list
flags.trigger: Any strike on a Saudi Red Sea port, a port closure notice, or a mandatory evacuation order from Saudi port authorities
